articles.title: US Ski Resorts Turn to Drones to Make It Snow Amid Dire Drought
articles.mainIdea: US Ski Resorts Turn to Drones to Make It Snow Amid Dire Drought
articles.summary: Bloomberg: US Ski Resorts Turn to Drones to Make It Snow Amid Dire Drought. When weather conditions are just right, a Winter Park contractor fires up the machine, burning a fine dust of silver iodide into the sky — a process known as cloud seeding. The silver iodide becomes the nuclei for water droplets, like iron filings to a magnet. Doug Laraby, who has helped run Winter Park for nearly four decades, says the resort leaned heavily on its cloud seeding equipment over the Christmas holiday, sprinkling the skies as fresh powder fell days before the critical New Years weekend. Related tickers mentioned: MT.
